'''DecipherCon 1999''' (DecipherCon '99) was Decipher's first company convention, held 11–14 November 1999 at the Cavalier Hotel, Virginia Beach, Virginia. It hosted the [[1999 Decipher World Championship|Star Wars CCG World Championship]], in which [[Gary Carman]] defeated [[Steven Lewis]] 2 (+19).<ref name="dc99-home">[http://www.decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/ DecipherCon 1999], Decipher. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20020823212712/http://www.decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/ Internet Archive]</ref><ref name="sw">[http://www.decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/swworldchamp/index.html Star Wars CCG World Championship], Decipher. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19991128144348/http://www.decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/swworldchamp/index.html Internet Archive]</ref> The same weekend hosted the [[Star Trek CCG]] World Championship, won by Mike Harrington, and the [[Young Jedi]] World Championship, won by [[Greg Heisler]].<ref name="lal-sat">[http://decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/lalumiere/saturday.html DecipherCon '99 — Day 3 Wrap-up], Francis K. Lalumiere, Decipher. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20001120012500/http://decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/lalumiere/saturday.html Internet Archive]</ref>

* '''Format:''' various: World Championship [[Premiere - Endor]]; side events in [[Japanese Sealed Deck]], [[Progressive Sealed Deck]], [[Players' Choice Sealed Deck]], [[Iron Man]], [[No Such Thing As Luck]], [[The Gauntlet: Dual Formats]], [[Allegiances: Multi-Deck Format]], [[Enhanced Format Sealed Deck]], [[EPP Overdrive]], and [[Team Event Format]]

== Registration and prizes ==

Online pre-registration ended on 31 October 1999. A pre-registered weekend pass cost $10, a 50% discount, and came with a free Young Jedi Menace of Darth Maul Sebulba foil card. Cavalier Hotel guests who pre-registered before 30 September got 10% off DecipherCon weekend room rates and one free pass per hotel confirmation. After 31 October, registration was at the door: $20 for a four-day pass or $10 for a one-day pass.<ref name="register">[http://www.decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/register.html DecipherCon pre-registration], Decipher (1999). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19991128100221/http://www.decipher.com:80/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/register.html Internet Archive]</ref>

Decipher's prize page listed uncut sheets from all of Decipher's card sets, original art from its art department, Japanese Star Wars CCG product, guest appearances on [[Radio Free Decipher]], complete card sets (including foil sets), complete sets of pre-released expansions, trophies, card t-shirts, and prize packages to summer 2000 conventions.<ref name="prizes">[http://www.decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/prizes.html DecipherCon prize details], Decipher (1999). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19991128083925/http://www.decipher.com:80/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/prizes.html Internet Archive]</ref>

[[Martin Akesson]] wrote that the Sunday team winners "got the coolest trophies!"<ref name="tr-d163">[https://www.stephenskilton.com/decktech_archives/reports/2000-01-09-world-championships-by-martin-akessond163/ world-championships-by-martin-akesson], DeckTech (Martin "Mart" Akesson, 9 January 2000). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261025134508/https://www.stephenskilton.com/decktech_archives/reports/2000-01-09-world-championships-by-martin-akessond163/ Internet Archive]</ref>

== Guests ==

Special guests were Chase Masterson (Leeta), [[Shannon Baksa]] (Mara Jade), [[Aron Eisenberg]] (Nog), and [[Jeremy Bulloch]] (Boba Fett). Signings ran Friday 1–3 p.m. and Saturday and Sunday 12–2 p.m., free for convention participants.<ref name="guests">[http://www.decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/specialguests/index.html Special guests], DecipherCon 1999, Decipher. == Star Wars CCG World Championship ==

Full results, lists, decks, and the Final Confrontation are on [[1999 Decipher World Championship]]. Lalumiere's live board coverage of the final is transcribed on [[1999 Decipher World Championship Final Confrontation]]. The constructed pool was [[Premiere - Endor]]. The field of 32 was 4 Open + 2 Invitational + 23 Regional + 2 Wild Card + 1 defending champion ([[Matt Potter]]).<ref name="field">[http://www.decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/swworldchamp/finalists.html Finalists], Decipher. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19991128125001/http://www.decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/swworldchamp/finalists.html Internet Archive]</ref>

Thursday's Wild Card Open (SW.01) put 147 players on Decipher's score sheet.<ref name="dc99sw01_1">[http://decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/events/scores/SW01_1.html DecipherCon 1999 – Event Scores: 1999 SW Wildcard], Decipher. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20011101231420/http://www.decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/events/scores/SW01_1.html Internet Archive]</ref> Lalumiere counted 146 Star Wars players that evening.<ref name="lal-thu">[http://decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/lalumiere/thursday.html DecipherCon '99 — Day 1 Wrap-up], Francis K. Lalumiere, Decipher. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20000903021929/http://www.decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/lalumiere/thursday.html Internet Archive]</ref> Decipher's thu01 photo caption gives 161.<ref name="thu01">[http://www.decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/photos/THU/thu01.html DecipherCon 1999 photo thu01], Decipher. Caption: "Wild Card players, 161 for Star Wars CCG and 61 for Star Trek CCG, will soon fill the room." Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20010119074700/http://www.decipher.com:80/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/photos/THU/thu01.html Internet Archive]</ref> The top two, [[John Arendt]] and [[James Lafferty]], took seats into Friday's field of 32.<ref name="dc99sw01_1" />

[[Joe Alread]] won Iron Man on Friday and missed the main event.<ref name="lal-fri">[http://decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/lalumiere/friday.html DecipherCon '99 — Day 2 Wrap-up], Francis K. Lalumiere, Decipher. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20001120001100/http://decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/lalumiere/friday.html Internet Archive]</ref> [[Kathy Lischke]] reported on Decipher's event board that his prize was a set of uncut Premiere sheets. Cards sent to the Lost Pile in that event went into a shredder.<ref name="kl-iron">[http://calder.decipher.com/cgi-bin/msgbd?dconerb$9521-11290$1 "Joe Alread: Ironman"], [[Kathy Lischke]], DecipherCon: Event Report Board, Decipher (12 November 1999). The archived copy is cut off mid-post. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20001025060303/http://calder.decipher.com:80/cgi-bin/msgbd?dconerb$9521-11290$1 Internet Archive]</ref>

On Saturday morning, Lischke reported, [[Gary Carman]] found that his planned decks were missing. He built two new decks with help from another qualifier and took them into the final.<ref name="kl-necessity">[http://calder.decipher.com/cgi-bin/msgbd?dconerb$10751-27562$1 "Necessity is the mother of invention"], [[Kathy Lischke]], DecipherCon: Event Report Board, Decipher (13 November 1999). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20001028020703/http://calder.decipher.com:80/cgi-bin/msgbd?dconerb$10751-27562$1 Internet Archive]</ref>

An ECC sealed event on Saturday drew 176 players by Lalumiere's count. He called it "the biggest tournament in Star Wars CCG history", ahead of the 152 at Origins constructed.<ref name="lal-sat">[http://decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/lalumiere/saturday.html DecipherCon '99 — Day 3 Wrap-up], Francis K. Lalumiere, Decipher. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20001120012500/http://decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/lalumiere/saturday.html Internet Archive]</ref> Decipher's photo captions give 162 and "160+".<ref name="sat58" /><ref name="sat68">[http://www.decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/photos/SAT/sat68.html DecipherCon 1999 photo sat68], Decipher. Caption: "Between rounds of the 160+ player Enhanced Cloud City tournament, Marcus Certa sings Broadway show tunes." Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20000602115340/http://www.decipher.com:80/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/photos/SAT/sat68.html Internet Archive]</ref>

== Star Wars CCG Team Championship ==

Sunday 14 November 1999 was the DecipherCon Team Challenge (SW.06), 10 a.m.–4 p.m.<ref name="dc99-sun">[http://decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/events/sun_events.html DecipherCon 1999 – Event Schedule: Sunday], Decipher. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20001026063736/http://decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/events/sun_events.html Internet Archive]</ref> A team of four won it: [[Martin Akesson]], [[Paul Todd Feldman]], [[Koen Meijssen]], and [[Yannick Lapointe]].<ref name="trando-iv7">[http://www.trandosite.mcmail.com/iv7.htm Martin Akesson interview], [[Trandosite]] (31 August 2000). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20041026204829/http://www.trandosite.mcmail.com/iv7.htm Internet Archive]</ref><ref name="drazin">[http://members.aol.com/drtorch/ErikDark.html Feldman's Drazin Deck: Decipher Con Team Play Winning Deck], Paul Todd Feldman, Torch Industries. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20000303173004/http://members.aol.com:80/drtorch/ErikDark.html Internet Archive]</ref> Full coverage is on [[DecipherCon 1999 Team Event]].

Akesson wrote that the team was "non americans +1". Bastian Winkelhaus and then Martin Falke were first named for the fourth seat. Both moved to other teams, and Feldman joined as the "+1".<ref name="tr-d163" /> Decipher's photo of the winners survives only as a small thumbnail ([[:File:DecipherCon 1999 Team Event winners sun24.gif|sun24]]).

== Seminars and other program ==

The Star Wars schedule listed a Deck Building Clinic (SW.41) on Thursday 6–8 p.m. and a Product Development seminar (SW.42) on Friday 11 a.m.–1 p.m.<ref name="dc99-thu">[http://decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/events/thu_events.html DecipherCon 1999 – Event Schedule: Thursday], Decipher. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20021005063305/http://www.decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/events/thu_events.html Internet Archive]</ref><ref name="dc99-fri">[http://decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/events/fri_events.html DecipherCon 1999 – Event Schedule: Friday], Decipher. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20000708001407/http://decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/events/fri_events.html Internet Archive]</ref> [[Chuck Kallenbach]] gave the Friday seminar on designing a Star Wars CCG expansion set, covering metagame adjustments, large mechanics, draw cards, the expanded universe and destiny numbers.<ref name="erb-expand">[http://calder.decipher.com/cgi-bin/msgbd?dconerb$254-22804$1 "Expand the Empire -- A Seminar on Designing Star Wars CCG"], Francis K. Lalumiere, DecipherCon: Event Report Board, Decipher (12 November 1999). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20001204063000/http://calder.decipher.com:80/cgi-bin/msgbd?dconerb$254-22804$1 Internet Archive]</ref> Lalumiere wrote that Friday also held a seminar on the evolution of a Star Trek CCG card from concept to print.<ref name="lal-fri">[http://decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/lalumiere/friday.html DecipherCon '99 — Day 2 Wrap-up], Francis K. Lalumiere, Decipher. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20001120001100/http://decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/lalumiere/friday.html Internet Archive]</ref> Celebrity signings ran Friday 1–3 p.m. and Saturday and Sunday 12–2 p.m.<ref name="guests">[http://www.decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/specialguests/index.html Special guests], DecipherCon 1999, Decipher. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20021005040225/http://www.decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/specialguests/index.html Internet Archive]</ref>

Decipher's convention home linked daily wrap-ups, a photo album, an event schedule with scores, special-guest pages, World Championship indexes, and related program pages.<ref name="dc99-home">[http://www.decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/ DecipherCon 1999], Decipher. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20020823212712/http://www.decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/ Internet Archive]</ref>

== Vote for the champ ==

Decipher asked fans on its website to pick the winners of the Star Wars CCG and Star Trek CCG World Championships, listing the finalists and Wild Card qualifiers of both. Of the more than 900 Star Wars CCG votes, Gary Ng and 10 others picked [[Gary Carman]]; Ng won a prize. Of the 500 Star Trek CCG votes, 8 picked Mike Harrington, and Shawn Reynolds was drawn from them. Each prize was the winner's choice of a display of Star Trek CCG Rules of Acquisition or one each of the four Enhanced Cloud City packs.<ref name="vote">[http://decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/vote.html Vote for the world champions: Their pick won, and so did they!], Decipher (1999). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20000120055420/http://decipher.com:80/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/vote.html Internet Archive]</ref>

== Radio Free Decipher ==

[[Radio Free Decipher]] talked about the convention before and after it. On Broadcast 26, recorded on Monday 27 September 1999, [[Kendrick Summers]] told [[Carol Wisely]] that he had visited the Cavalier the week before to look at the space. He said the top two players from the Thursday Star Wars Wild Card would join Friday's Day One, and the top 12 from Friday would play Saturday's final rounds.<ref name="rfd26">[http://www.decipher.com/rfd/archives/audio/rfd_99_09_27.ra Radio Free Decipher, Broadcast 26 (27 September 1999)], [[Carol Wisely]] with [[Kendrick Summers]], Decipher, 2:02–2:30 and 8:14–8:40. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20000903024602/http://www.decipher.com/rfd/archives/audio/rfd_99_09_27.ra Internet Archive]</ref> Broadcast 27 (8 October 1999), hosted by [[Marcus Certa]] and [[Ryan Morris]], named [[Aron Eisenberg]] and [[Jeremy Bulloch]] among the expected guests.<ref name="rfd-list99">[http://www.decipher.com/rfd/archives/index1998-99.html RFD Archives 1998-1999 – Broadcasts 1-30], Decipher. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20081207011923/http://www.decipher.com/rfd/archives/index1998-99.html Internet Archive]</ref><ref name="rfd27">[http://www.decipher.com/rfd/archives/audio/rfd_99_10_08.ra Radio Free Decipher, Broadcast 27 (8 October 1999)], Decipher, 7:04–7:35. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20000903024542/http://www.decipher.com/rfd/archives/audio/rfd_99_10_08.ra Internet Archive]</ref> The archive's list of broadcasts also has a special, ''The Sounds of DecipherCon '99'', with "over sixty big audio bites" from the weekend. Its link went to the convention site.<ref name="rfd-list99" />

On Broadcast 24 (3 September 1999), [[Kendrick Summers]] told [[Carol Wisely]] the convention would run 11–14 November at the Cavalier, with nearly the whole hotel used for gaming and seminars and gaming around the clock. Guests who booked at the Cavalier before 30 September got 10% off and a free pass. Other weekend passes cost $10 until 31 October and $20 at the door. The prizes would include team trophies, and the Austin Powers CCG would have fun tournaments with team events.<ref name="rfd24">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PBEi5cn8qds Broadcast 24 - Radio Free Decipher (03 September, 1999): Kendrick Summers, Evan Lorentz, Juz Pakes], Player's Council (YouTube), 1:10–2:55, 5:39–5:58, 11:04–11:50 and 15:35–15:48. Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-PBEi5cn8qds Internet Archive]</ref>

On Broadcast 29 (29 October 1999), [[Marcus Certa]] and [[Evan Lorentz]] said Decipher hoped to pre-release ''Star Trek'' CCG Rules of Acquisition at the convention, and that Enhanced Cloud City would have its first American pre-release there. They counted more than a dozen tournament types exclusive to the convention, among them Galactic Supremacy for ''Star Trek'', in which everyone playing an affiliation formed one team, and an Iron Man event. Young Jedi had its Open World Championship, and Austin Powers CCG demonstrations would show multiplayer games. Lorentz would judge the ''Star Trek'' World Championship. Online pre-registration closed that Sunday and cost $10 for the weekend. At the door a weekend pass was $20 and day passes $10.<ref name="rfd29">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4Wci5TkoXNg Broadcast 29 - Radio Free Decipher (29 October, 1999): Evan Lorentz on DecipherCon and CCG News], Player's Council (YouTube), 4:03–4:13, 8:38–8:55, 11:37–12:09, 13:45–14:17 and 21:20–22:31. Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-4Wci5TkoXNg Internet Archive]</ref>

After the convention, Broadcast 30 (3 December 1999) said DecipherCon players had taken part in the trial run of the Austin Powers events that the Austin Powers Road Tour was then running.<ref name="rfd30">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=iGgiAkH-fd0 Broadcast 30 - Radio Free Decipher (03 December, 1999): Kyle Heuer, Marcus Certa on Austin Powers], Player's Council (YouTube), 2:26–3:03. Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-iGgiAkH-fd0 Internet Archive]</ref>

On Broadcast 38 (16 June 2000), [[Evan Lorentz]] and [[Kyle Heuer]] interviewed [[Gary Carman]] by phone from Bristol. They said the final had been shown on closed-circuit television at the convention and that the room where it was played was "quiet as death". Carman called it "definitely a pressure factor".<ref name="rfd38">[http://www.decipher.com/rfd/archives/audio/rfd_00_06_16.ra Radio Free Decipher, Broadcast 38 (16 June 2000)], [[Evan Lorentz]] and [[Kyle Heuer]], Decipher, 0:23–0:36 and 7:19–8:20. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20000903024158/http://www.decipher.com/rfd/archives/audio/rfd_00_06_16.ra Internet Archive]</ref>

=== Radio Free DecipherCon ===

[[File:Ryan Morris and Mark Tuttle DecipherCon 1999.gif|thumb|right|[[Ryan Morris]] and [[Mark Tuttle]], Radio Free DecipherCon]]
During the convention [[Ryan Morris]] and [[Mark Tuttle]] ran the Radio Free DecipherCon audio feeds from the floor.<ref name="dc99-audio">[http://www.decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/audiofeeds/index.html DecipherCon 1999 audio feeds], Decipher (1999): "Meet Ryan Morris and Mark Tuttle! - the voice and tech behind Radio Free DecipherCon." Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20021005044012/http://www.decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/audiofeeds/index.html Internet Archive].</ref> Thursday's feeds have interviews with [[Evan Lorentz]], [[Chuck Kallenbach]] and Star Wars CCG finalists.<ref name="dc99-audio-thu">[http://www1.decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/audiofeeds/THU/index.html DecipherCon 1999 audio feeds: Thursday], Decipher (1999). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20010217093703/http://www1.decipher.com:80/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/audiofeeds/THU/index.html Internet Archive].</ref> Friday's have [[Jeremy Bulloch]], [[Shannon Baksa]] and round updates.<ref name="dc99-audio-fri">[http://www1.decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/audiofeeds/FRI/index.html DecipherCon 1999 audio feeds: Friday], Decipher (1999). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20010217084830/http://www1.decipher.com:80/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/audiofeeds/FRI/index.html Internet Archive].</ref> Saturday's carry play-by-play and interviews from the three World Championship finals.<ref name="dc99-audio-sat">[http://decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/audiofeeds/SAT/index.html DecipherCon 1999 audio feeds: Saturday], Decipher (1999). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20000313011020/http://decipher.com:80/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/audiofeeds/SAT/index.html Internet Archive].</ref> Sunday's announce the winners and end with Tuttle and Morris's closing comments.<ref name="dc99-audio-sun">[http://www1.decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/audiofeeds/SUN/index.html DecipherCon 1999 audio feeds: Sunday], Decipher (1999): "Closing comments....and that's all folks (M. Tuttle, R. Morris)". Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20010217090821/http://www1.decipher.com:80/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/audiofeeds/SUN/index.html Internet Archive].</ref>

== Trip reports ==

=== Daily wrap-ups ===

[[Francis Lalumiere|Francis K. Lalumiere]] wrote official daily wrap-ups for Thursday through Sunday.

* Day 1 (Thursday): the Wild Card tournaments, about a dozen formats, and the paper shredders of the Star Trek Iron Man event.<ref name="lal-thu">[http://decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/lalumiere/thursday.html DecipherCon '99 — Day 1 Wrap-up], Francis K. Lalumiere, Decipher. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20000903021929/http://www.decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/lalumiere/thursday.html Internet Archive]</ref>
* Day 2 (Friday): the first phase of the Star Wars and Star Trek championships, the first Young Jedi qualifier, and the guests' first signings.<ref name="lal-fri">[http://decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/lalumiere/friday.html DecipherCon '99 — Day 2 Wrap-up], Francis K. Lalumiere, Decipher. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20001120001100/http://decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/lalumiere/friday.html Internet Archive]</ref>
* Day 3 (Saturday): the three World Championship finals and the Enhanced Cloud City sealed event, which he put at 176 players.<ref name="lal-sat">[http://decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/lalumiere/saturday.html DecipherCon '99 — Day 3 Wrap-up], Francis K. Lalumiere, Decipher. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20001120012500/http://decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/lalumiere/saturday.html Internet Archive]</ref>
* Day 4 (Sunday): the gaming halls growing quiet on Sunday afternoon as players left, and the convention's international mix.<ref name="lal-sun">[http://decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/lalumiere/index.html DecipherCon '99 — Day 4 Wrap-up], Francis K. Lalumiere, Decipher. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20000122055105/http://decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/lalumiere/index.html Internet Archive]</ref>

=== Other reports ===

''[[Star Wars Insider]]'' 48 carried [[Richard Handley]]'s report "[[All Decked Out (Star Wars Insider)|All Decked Out]]" on the Star Wars CCG World Championship and the first [[Young Jedi]] World Championship.<ref name="swi48">Rich Handley, "All Decked Out", ''Star Wars Insider'' 48 (2000), pp. 78–79; listed in the contents as "Decipher This!". Scan: [https://archive.org/details/star-wars-insider-56b702/page/n81/mode/2up Internet Archive].</ref>

Player reports from the weekend include:

* [[Martin Akesson World Championships by Martin Akesson (tournament report)]] — Worlds, Progressive Sealed, Japanese Sealed, Enhanced Sealed, and the team event
* [[Matt Lush Day One World Championships (tournament report)]] — Worlds Day 1 and Saturday sealed play

== Discrepancies ==

* Wild Card Open (SW.01) players: 147 on Decipher's score sheet,<ref name="dc99sw01_1" /> 146 in Lalumiere's Day 1 wrap-up,<ref name="lal-thu" /> and 161 in the thu01 photo caption.<ref name="thu01" />
* Enhanced Cloud City sealed players: 176 in Lalumiere's Day 3 wrap-up,<ref name="lal-sat" /> 162 in the sat58 photo caption<ref name="sat58" /> and "160+" in the sat68 caption.<ref name="sat68" />
